newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli shekel rises against dollar, basket.
newsitem.headline: Israeli shekel rises against dollar, basket.

text.p: The Israeli shekel rose on Monday against the dollar and the basket of key foreign currencies following the decline of the U.S. currency in Europe, dealers said.
"Activity was high and mixed today. The shekel rose against the dollar following the dollar's decline abroad," said Guy Levi a dealer at Bank Leumi.
"The release of October's consumer price index (last Friday) had no impact on trading since the Bank of Israel is not expected to lower interest rates," Levi added.
The CPI rose 0.8 percent in October against an increase of 0.4 percent in September.

The representative rate for the dollar was fixed at 3.2270 shekels against 3.2350 on Friday. The basket, composed of the dollar, mark, pound sterling, French franc and yen, closed at 3.6357 shekels against 3.6442 on Friday.
On the crosses the shekel traded against the yen at 2.8930 shekels per 100 yen against 2.8968 on Friday and against the mark at 2.1414 shekels against 2.1470 on Friday.
In late afternoon the dollar was trading at 3.2260 shekels.
